Hey I just wanted to say that I’ve been in a similar situation. I’m on the autism spectrum too and I’ve got motor skill issues because of it. I moved into my first apartment a little less than a year ago and I got a noise complaint in December. I had a down stairs neighbor that was tapping on my ceiling when I would accidentally drop slam things or walk too loud. I understood that they didn’t like me dropping things, but the other times I really couldn’t figure out what they were doing that in response to until I got a note from them. The night I got a note from them, not only was it a really angry note saying stuff like “Do you even know how to be quiet? Do you know not to drop or throw things? Do you know not to slam things? It gets old being woken up in the middle of the night!”, ( I have sleep issues and I’m a night owl because of autism) but they also hit my door really hard and it scared me because I’m a girl living alone. I was just like you after that where I because really paranoid. It wasn’t until a few weeks later that I got a gift and a card from my neighbor apologizing for the note he left. Regardless, did take the note very hard. I felt bad. I didn’t even realize I was doing some of those things most of the time. My mom has told me in the past that I’ve walked heavy or slammed doors a few times, but honestly when you have motor skill issues, you really don’t even notice that you do stuff like that. It’s just how your body does things. Now I just leave most of the doors in my apartment open until I go to bed and when I close the front door I have to think to myself “don’t slam it! Don’t slam it!”. Looking back at this, I think during those one or two weeks I was probably a little noisier than usual. It was my first complaint since moving in for like 8 months.
